newsitem.title: NORWAY: Shell to begin exploration off mid-Norway in AugusT.
newsitem.headline: Shell to begin exploration off mid-Norway in AugusT.

text.p: Norske Shell will begin spudding an exploration well on licence 214 in the Vegahoegda area off mid-Norway in August, its first well on acreage awarded in the 15th licensing round, the company said on Monday.
The well will be spudded in water depth of 320 metres and will be drilled down to 4,500 metres below sea level. Drilling is scheduled to run from mid-August to December.

The company's newsletter, Nytt fra Shell, said the large geological structure in the area on blocks 6510/1 and 6510/2 has been known for many years but without any certainty over what resources it could contain. The Vega well would be the most important exploration drilling for Shell from many years, it said.
Shell geologist Andreas Lunde said new geological models had increased the possibility that there were oil and gas formations in the area.

"If the result of the first well is positive, we will consider carrying out an appraisal well immediately. That is important to decide whether it's worth continuing work on the find, a production solution and seismic methodology," Lunde was quoted as saying.
Shell spokesman Terje Jonassen said the exploration was high risk.
"This is a high risk type of well geologically speaking with around a 10 percent possibility of success," Jonassen told Reuters.
Shell, as operator, holds 30 percent of licence 214 and is partnered by Elf and Mobil with 20 percent. The Norwegian state's direct financial interest is 30 percent.

Jonassen said the company would begin spudding its first exploration well on production licence 210 also off mid-Norway in December. This licence was the second operatorship Shell was awarded in the 15th round.
